biography.plain_text: Joseph Sicari is an American vision-products entrepreneur who acquired Paragon Vision Sciences with Summit Partners after becoming its president. His business supplied specialist contact lenses and oxygen-permeable lens materials. He later reacquired Paragon from Valeant and sold it to CooperVision. He is a graduate of the College of William & Mary.

long_biography.plain_text:
Joseph Sicari helped bring overnight vision correction to market. At Paragon, he led the launch of corneal reshaping lenses worn overnight, which temporarily alter the cornea's curvature to correct nearsightedness.

He subsequently partnered with optometrist Alan Reichow to develop a single-use successor to the MaxSight contact lens, leading to the launch of ALTIUS. His involvement also extended to invention: he is a named co-inventor on a patent application combining tinted lenses with separate optical zones for clear vision and defocus. The design seeks to slow myopia progression while addressing the blurred sensation associated with defocus lenses.
